rationale: A wins because it gives the founder more real routes to coverage: labor data, IPO disclosure, worker-accountability, consumer harm, and enterprise-AI ROI are not the same story in different shoes. Its strongest line, "Klarna won't say how many of the jobs it cut were actually replaced by AI," is over-headlined but correctly spots the accountability hole B mostly tucks inside other angles. B is cleaner about proof, but "When your BNPL dispute is decided by a chatbot" commits the factual overreach it then lectures against. Slight win: A is better strategic material, but it still needs headline surgery before anyone sends it.
gaps_in_A: "Klarna won't say how many of the jobs it cut were actually replaced by AI" overstates the facts. The update says headcount fell, partly through attrition, and Klarna will not disclose roles cut versus left unfilled; it does not establish AI replacement of cut jobs.

"Klarna's AI is now handling disputes for a base of 150 million consumers" overreaches. The facts say Klarna processes payments for 150 million consumers and advocates raised concerns about AI handling disputes, not that the AI handles disputes for that whole base.

"The most-mocked category of enterprise AI might actually be working" imports a broad reputation claim not in the update, then says "two-thirds resolved" when the supplied fact is only that the assistant handles two-thirds of chats.
The repeated "24hr" decay and "same window as Klarna's IPO filing" language treats the IPO filing as a fresh timed peg without a supplied filing date.
gaps_in_B: "When your BNPL dispute is decided by a chatbot" asserts the chatbot decides disputes. The update only says advocates raised concerns about AI handling disputes; B knows this, because its proof section asks whether disputes are handled or escalated.

"Klarna cut average chat resolution from 11 minutes to under 2 — here's how" promises an operational how-to, but the update supplies no workflow, guardrails, product lead, customer case, or implementation detail.

"A profitable, IPO-bound Klarna leans on AI it won't fully explain" leans harder on AI dependency than the facts allow. Profitability, IPO filing, and AI support metrics are supplied; an AI-dependent profitability story is not.
The next step, "newsjack-detector," sends the founder backward. After these angles, the useful move is sourcing the proof gaps and running journalist-fit-check on the chosen angle.
